__PERSON_F__ Is __MASTER_A__ of the Sabbath
1 One Sabbath __PERSON_F__ was going through the grainfields, and his disciples began to pick some heads of grain, rub them in their hands and eat the kernels. 2 Some of the Pharisees asked, “Why are you doing what is unlawful on the Sabbath?”

3 __PERSON_F__ answered them, “Have you never read what __KING_A__ did when he and his companions were hungry? 4 He entered the house of __MOST_HIGH_A__, and taking the consecrated bread, he ate what is lawful only for __WORKER_A__ to eat. And he also gave some to his companions.” 5 Then __PERSON_F__ said to them, “The Son of Man is __MASTER_A__ of the Sabbath.”

1 On another Sabbath he went into the synagogue and was teaching, and a man was there whose right hand was shriveled. 7 The Pharisees and the teachers of the law were looking for a reason to accuse __PERSON_F__, so they watched him closely to see if he would heal on the Sabbath. 8 But __PERSON_F__ knew what they were thinking and said to the man with the shriveled hand, “Get up and stand in front of everyone.” So he got up and stood there.

9 Then __PERSON_F__ said to them, “I ask you, which is lawful on the Sabbath: to do good or to do evil, to save life or to destroy it?”

10 He looked around at them all, and then said to the man, “Stretch out your hand.” He did so, and his hand was completely restored. 11 But the Pharisees and the teachers of the law were furious and began to discuss with one another what they might do to __PERSON_F__.

The Twelve Apostles
12 One of those days __PERSON_F__ went out to a mountainside to pray, and spent the night __REQUEST_A__ to __MOST_HIGH_A__. 13 When morning came, he called his disciples to him and chose twelve of them, whom he also designated apostles: 14 Simon (whom he named Peter), his brother Andrew, James, __PERSON_C__, Philip, Bartholomew, 15 Matthew, Thomas, James son of Alphaeus, Simon who was called the Zealot, 16 Judas son of James, and Judas Iscariot, who became a traitor.

Blessings and Woes
17 He went down with them and stood on a level place. A large crowd of his disciples was there and a great number of people from all over Judea, from __CITY_A__, and from the coastal region around Tyre and Sidon, 18 who had come to hear him and to be healed of their diseases. Those troubled by impure spirits were cured, 19 and the people all tried to touch him, because power was coming from him and healing them all.

20 Looking at his disciples, he said:

“Blessed are you who are poor,
for yours is the kingdom of __MOST_HIGH_A__.
21 Blessed are you who hunger now,
for you will be satisfied.
Blessed are you who weep now,
for you will laugh.
22 Blessed are you when people hate you,
when they exclude you and insult you
and reject your name as evil,
because of the Son of Man.

23 “Rejoice in that day and leap for joy, because great is your reward in heaven. For that is how their ancestors treated the prophets.

24 “But woe to you who are rich,
for you have already received your comfort.
25 Woe to you who are well fed now,
for you will go hungry.
Woe to you who laugh now,
for you will mourn and weep.
26 Woe to you when everyone speaks well of you,
for that is how their ancestors treated the false prophets.

Love for Enemies
27 “But to you who are listening I say: Love your enemies, do good to those who hate you, 28 bless those who curse you, pray for those who mistreat you. 29 If someone slaps you on one cheek, turn to them the other also. If someone takes your coat, do not withhold your shirt from them. 30 Give to everyone who asks you, and if anyone takes what belongs to you, do not demand it back. 31 Do to others as you would have them do to you.

32 “If you love those who love you, what credit is that to you? Even sinners love those who love them. 33 And if you do good to those who are good to you, what credit is that to you? Even sinners do that. 34 And if you lend to those from whom you expect repayment, what credit is that to you? Even sinners lend to sinners, expecting to be repaid in full. 35 But love your enemies, do good to them, and lend to them without expecting to get anything back. Then your reward will be great, and you will be children of the __HONORED_A__, because he is kind to the ungrateful and wicked. 36 Be merciful, just as your Father is merciful.

Judging Others
37 “Do not judge, and you will not be judged. Do not condemn, and you will not be condemned. Forgive, and you will be forgiven. 38 Give, and it will be given to you. A good measure, pressed down, shaken together and running over, will be poured into your lap. For with the measure you use, it will be measured to you.”

39 He also told them this parable: “Can the blind lead the blind? Will they not both fall into a pit? 40 The student is not above the teacher, but everyone who is fully trained will be like their teacher.

41 “Why do you look at the speck of sawdust in your brother’s eye and pay no attention to the plank in your own eye? 42 How can you say to your brother, ‘Brother, let me take the speck out of your eye,’ when you yourself fail to see the plank in your own eye? You hypocrite, first take the plank out of your eye, and then you will see clearly to remove the speck from your brother’s eye.

A Tree and Its Fruit
43 “No good tree bears bad fruit, nor does a bad tree bear good fruit. 44 Each tree is recognized by its own fruit. People do not pick figs from thornbushes, or grapes from briers. 45 A good man brings good things out of the good stored up in his heart, and an evil man brings evil things out of the evil stored up in his heart. For the mouth speaks what the heart is full of.

The Wise and Foolish Builders
46 “Why do you call me, ‘__MASTER_A__, __MASTER_A__,’ and do not do what I say? 47 As for everyone who comes to me and hears my words and puts them into practice, I will show you what they are like. 48 They are like a man building a house, who dug down deep and laid the foundation on rock. When a flood came, the torrent struck that house but could not shake it, because it was well built. 49 But the one who hears my words and does not put them into practice is like a man who built a house on the ground without a foundation. The moment the torrent struck that house, it collapsed and its destruction was complete.”
translations:
__PERSON_F__ 是安息日的 __MASTER_A__  
1 有一天安息日，__PERSON_F__ 走过麦田，他的门徒开始摘麦穗，在手里揉搓，吃里面的籽。 2 有些法利赛人问：“你为什么安息日做不合法的事？”  

3 __PERSON_F__ 回答说：“你们没读过 __KING_A__ 一次和同伴饿的时候做了什么吗？ 4 他进了 __MOST_HIGH_A__ 的屋子，取了圣饼，那是只有 __WORKER_A__ 才合法吃的，他吃了，也给同伴吃。” 5 然后 __PERSON_F__ 对他们说：“人子是安息日的 __MASTER_A__。”  

1 另一天安息日，他进会堂教导，有个人右手枯干。 7 法利赛人和律法师找机会控告 __PERSON_F__，盯着看他安息日是否治病。 8 但 __PERSON_F__ 知道他们想什么，就对那个枯手的人说：“站起来，站在众人前。” 他就起来站着。  

9 __PERSON_F__ 对他们说：“我问你们，安息日做什么合法：做好事还是作恶，救生命还是毁灭？”  

10 他环顾众人，对那人说：“伸手。” 他伸手，手完全恢复了。11 法利赛人和律法师很生气，商量如何对付 __PERSON_F__。  

十二使徒  
12 有一天，__PERSON_F__ 去山上祷告，并整夜 __REQUEST_A__ 给 __MOST_HIGH_A__。 13 天亮，他叫门徒，拣选十二个，称为使徒：14 西门（他取名彼得），他的兄弟安得烈，雅各，__PERSON_C__，腓力，巴多罗买，15 马太，多马，亚勒腓的儿子雅各，被称为奋锐党的西门，16 雅各的儿子犹大，加略人犹大，就是卖主的。  

祝福和祸哉  
17 他和他们下山，站在平地。大群门徒和很多犹太各地、__CITY_A__、推罗西顿海边地区的人都来听他教，求医治。18 被污灵困扰的人得医治，19 人人都想摸他，因为能力从他出来，医治众人。  

20 看着门徒他说：  

“你们贫穷的人有福了，  
因为你们是 __MOST_HIGH_A__ 的国民。  
21 现在饥饿的人有福了，  
你们必得满足。哭泣的人有福了，  
你们必欢笑。  
22 当人恨你们，排斥你们，辱骂你们，弃绝你们的时候，因人子，你们有福了。  

23 “你们就在那日欢喜踊跃，因为你们天上的赏赐大。他们祖先也是这样待先知的。  

24 “但富有的人有祸了，  
因为你们已经得了安慰。  
25 吃饱的人有祸了，  
你们必饥饿。现在欢笑的有祸了，  
你们必悲哀哭泣。  
26 人人说你们好有祸了，  
因为你们祖先也是这样待假先知的。  

爱你的敌人  
27 “但我告诉听的人：爱你们的敌人，善待恨你的人，28 祝福咒诅你的人，为虐待你的人祷告。 29 有人打你脸一边，连另一边也转给他。有人夺你外衣，不要阻止他拿里面的衬衣。30 凡求你的，就给他。有人拿了你的东西，不要求回。31 你们愿意人怎样待你们，你们也怎样待人。  

32 “你们如果爱爱你们的人，算不得什么？罪人也爱爱他们的人。33 你们如果善待善待你们的人，也算不得什么？罪人也这样做。34 你们如果借贷只求偿还，也算不得什么？罪人也借给罪人，期待全数收回。35 你们倒要爱敌人，善待他们，无条件借贷，赏赐就大，你们是 __HONORED_A__ 的儿女，因为他善待忘恩和恶人。36 要有怜悯，像你们的父是怜悯的。  

断别人  
37 “不要论断，就不被论断。不要定罪，就不被定罪。饶恕，就必蒙饶恕。38 施舍，就得施舍。用满着挤压摇动满溢的量倒入你怀里。因为用什么量给人，也必用什么量给你。”  

39 他也讲比喻说：“盲人能领盲人吗？不是都要掉坑里吗？40 门徒不能高过老师，凡完全训练的，必像老师。  

41 “你为何看见你弟兄眼中的木屑，却不想自己眼中的梁木？42 你怎么对弟兄说‘让我把你眼中的木屑去掉’，自己不看自己眼中的梁木呢？假冒为善的人，先去掉自己眼中梁木，然后才能看清去掉弟兄眼中的木屑。  

一棵树和它的果子  
43 “好树不结坏果，坏树不结好果。44 树凭果子认出。人不从荆棘摘无花果，不从蒺藜摘葡萄。45 好人从心里储存的善，发出善来。坏人从恶心发恶来。口里所出是心里所满。  

聪明和愚笨的盖房人  
46 “你们为什么叫我‘__MASTER_A__, __MASTER_A__’，却不遵行我说的话？47 凡来听我话又遵行的，我给你们比方：48 犹如盖房子的人，挖地根基，立磐石。洪水来，水流冲那房子，不能动，因为立得稳。49 听了不行的，好像无根基盖房子。洪水一来，房子坍塌，毁坏完全。”
